title: How to help an ageing parent remember the important things
description: Tablets, appointments, bin day and bills. Practical ways to help a parent remember what matters, without taking over their life or calling all day.
imageAlt: A WhatsApp reminder from Emily to her mum saying Take your tablet, with a Done button

title: How to set reminders on WhatsApp, for you and for someone else
description: What WhatsApp can and can't do with reminders, the simple ways to remind yourself, and how to send reminders to someone else that they actually act on.
imageAlt: A WhatsApp chat showing a reminder to put the bins out, with a Done button

title: Living alone safely: a practical guide
description: Simple things to set up when you live alone, so someone would notice if something went wrong, without giving up any of the freedom you moved out for.
imageAlt: A daily I'm OK message on WhatsApp with an I'm OK button

title: How to remind an elderly parent to take their medication
description: Practical ways to help a parent remember their tablets, from pill organisers and pharmacy help to reminders they can answer, without taking over.
imageAlt: A WhatsApp reminder from Emily to her mum saying "Take your morning tablets", with a Done button

title: Clocks go back on 25 October: a checklist for you and your parents
description: The clocks go back at 2am on Sunday 25 October. A short checklist for you and your parents, from clocks and medicines to smoke alarms and darker evenings.
imageAlt: A WhatsApp reminder saying "Clocks went back last night. Check the oven and car clocks", with a Done button

title: Shared reminders for couples and flatmates
description: How to stop one person remembering everything at home. A fair way to share bins, bills, rent and chores, with reminders that come from the system, not from you.
imageAlt: A WhatsApp reminder from Emily to Sam saying "Bins out tonight", with a Done button and Sam's reply "Done

title: How to remind someone without nagging
description: How to remind your partner, parent or teenager without sounding like a nag. What makes reminders feel like care rather than criticism, with examples.
imageAlt: A WhatsApp reminder from I'm OK saying "Bins out tonight" with a Done button, and the reply "Done

title: What is a safety word, and how do you use one?
description: A safety word is a secret word that tells the people you trust you need help, without anyone else knowing. How it works, when to use one, and how to set one up.
imageAlt: A WhatsApp chat where John sends the word "pumpkin" and I'm OK replies with a thumbs up and a Send location button

title: Caring for a parent from abroad
description: Living in a different country from your parents? Practical ways to stay involved, from a local support network and paperwork to daily signs that all is well.
imageAlt: A WhatsApp reminder from Emily to Mum saying "Take your tablet", with a Done button and Mum's reply "Done"
